contracts.contract: Local task and milestone IDs remain authoritative; redacted GitHub URLs are counterparts only. Failed synchronization preserves local state and produces an actionable retry marker.
contracts.example: service-booking-2-build-backend-foundation maps to one issue under service-booking-2-foundation; closing that issue cannot complete the local task.

contracts.contract: The versioned OpenAPI document and architecture boundary record define account roles, simulated adapters, same-origin session and CSRF behavior, data ownership, Swiss-storage nonclaim, and error shapes before dependent implementation starts.
contracts.example: POST /api/auth/provider/register creates only a provider identity; publication remains unavailable until simulated verification succeeds.

contracts.contract: The flow record defines anonymous, customer, provider, verified and unverified states; English/German selection and device-local persistence; labels, keyboard operation, validation states, and 390px/1280px behavior.
contracts.example: Unsupported browser language selects English; the visible language switch changes UI copy and persists only on the current device.

contracts.contract: The Spring Boot API implements the accepted OpenAPI surface with PostgreSQL/Flyway state, non-reversible password hashes, same-origin secure HTTP-only sessions, CSRF enforcement, role separation, and replaceable verification/reset adapters.
contracts.example: An anonymous cart mutation returns the declared unauthenticated error; an unverified customer reserve attempt returns the declared verification-required error.

contracts.contract: The React shell consumes only the accepted OpenAPI and flow contracts, sends CSRF-protected same-origin requests, exposes role-bound navigation, and uses English/German resource keys without translating provider-authored content.
contracts.example: A provider account never sees customer cart actions, and switching to German changes interface copy without rewriting provider-authored text.

contracts.contract: Code Review, Build Verification, Quality Review, and Independent Audit run in that order against one exact candidate. Any candidate change repeats affected gates; the human milestone decision remains separate and final.
contracts.example: A correction after Code Review creates a new candidate digest, invalidating later gate evidence for the previous candidate.
